title: AI, Probability and Learning from Data
status: Draft practice quiz; teacher review required
instructions: Ten questions: five on AI and learning, five on probability and uncertain evidence. Multiple-choice items require every correct option. One point for an exact match.

questions.prompt: What makes a fixed thermostat different from a learning system?
options: It explicitly follows a temperature condition
It needs labelled pictures to run
It predicts weather from big datasets
It always uses a neural network
questions.explanation: A conventional thermostat checks a rule written by a person.

questions.prompt: A program explores possible paths in a maze until it finds an exit. Which approach is most directly illustrated?
questions.explanation: A maze solver explores possible states and paths according to rules; it need not be trained.

questions.prompt: A table contains temperature, time of day and the user's desired heating state. What is the target label?
questions.explanation: In supervised learning, the known desired output is the label.

questions.prompt: Six unlabelled objects are divided into two groups by similarity. Which type of learning is this?
questions.explanation: Clustering seeks structure without supplied class labels.

questions.prompt: An agent learns which move to take by receiving rewards after actions. Which training setup does this describe?
questions.explanation: Reinforcement learning uses reward feedback to improve actions/policies.

questions.prompt: You guess one face of a fair ten-sided die. You are told that the rolled face is even. If your guessed face was 4, what is the probability you guessed correctly?
questions.explanation: The even-number condition leaves five possible results: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Only one matches face 4, so P(4 | even) = 1/5.

questions.prompt: In the fictional class of 100, 60 know the true/false answer and the remaining 40 guess. If a correct answer is observed, what is P(knew | correct)?
questions.explanation: All 60 who know answer correctly, and 20 of the 40 who guess are correct on average. Of the 80 correct answers, 60 came from knowledge: 60/80 = 75%.

questions.prompt: What is the expected value of the face shown by a fair ten-sided die labelled 1 to 10?
questions.explanation: Each face has probability 0.1, so E[X] = (1 + 2 + ... + 10)/10 = 55/10 = 5.5.

questions.prompt: Select ALL correct statements about the Week 1 Bayes experiment.
options: In the simplified model, P(correct | knew) = 100%.
P(knew | correct) always equals P(correct | knew).
For the initial 60% who know, P(knew | correct) = 75%.
A correct true/false answer proves the pupil knew.
questions.explanation: We assume someone who knows answers correctly, but some guesses are correct too. Reversing the given condition changes the probability.

questions.prompt: Select ALL conclusions supported by the fair-versus-tricky ten-sided die experiments.
options: The fair and tricky distributions both have expected value 5.5.
Two different distributions can have the same expected value.
If 30 rolls have average 5.5, the die must be fair.
Every sample of 30 rolls must exactly match the probability distribution.
questions.explanation: The fair die is uniform; the tricky die favours 1 and 10. Both have the same mean 5.5, but their distributions differ, and finite samples vary.
